A letter from #ManCity chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak. ⤵️

I have been part of this Club for 18 years. I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul. This Club matters to me, and you have shown and told me – time and time again - how much Manchester City matters to you. This is why I am writing to you today. 

Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023 (also below). Every word matters and holds true.

While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris St Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium - moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family.

Thank you, as always, for your constant support.

Khaldoon Al Mubarak

Chairman

Manchester City Football Club

The following letters have been attached to the latest statement from the club’s chairman:

Club Statement Friday 25th September 2026

The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

Club Statement February 2023

Manchester City FC is surprised by the issuing of these alleged breaches of the Premier League Rules, particularly given the extensive engagement and vast amount of detailed materials that the EPL has been provided with.

The Club welcomes the review of this matter by an independent Commission, to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position.

As such we look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.

RT @BakchodFpl: 🎯 "Routes to Points" - who's got the most paths to FPL returns (GW1-GW5)?

Checked 153 players with 300+ mins across 6 key metrics, and counted how many metrics each player beats the average on:

- Mins
- xCS/90
- Defcon/90
- BPS/90
- xGI/90
- Set pieces/90 (corners + free-kicks/90)

This list covers everyone hitting at least 4/6 routes mentioned above.

Standouts:

🔹Tavernier and Szoboszlai are the only two at a perfect 6/6 - but interestingly Tavernier's numbers are the more impressive of the pair, ahead on most of the individual metrics.

🔹The list is dominated by midfielders - only 3 defenders make the cut (Guéhi, Hall, De Cuyper), which says a lot about how strong those defensive picks are right now.

A few names in the 5-routes tier are surprising inclusions - Wirtz, McAtee and Tielemans weren't the first players you'd expect to see there, but the underlying numbers back it up.

Enzo Maresca: "I spoke with Pep [Guardiola] after the [Manchester] United game, I didn't speak with him after that. Enzo Maresca: "The message for tomorrow night is quite easy: We need the perfect game because they are the best team in Europe in this moment, they won the last two #UCL's, so that shows how good they are! Enzo Maresca: "I'm excited for tomorrow night because I was here in the Treble season, and I know that the #UCL nights are special, and hopefully tomorrow night can be special too!"

Enzo Maresca: "I think we are, for sure, a good team - no doubts about that! Where we are in this moment compared to PSG? I don't know, to be honest. I know how good they are because in the last two years they won the last two #UCL's, that shows how good they are. But at the same time, I don't know if we are close, far, where we are, but for sure we are a good team!"

Enzo Maresca on criticism for #ManCity's celebrations at Anfield: "Criticised for what? We won 0-3 at Anfield! What do you want us to do? And even if it was 0-1, it would be exactly the same.

"I'm here today, and the players are here today, to win tomorrow's game. And we work every day to win games. It's the only thing, again, that we can think and be focussed.

"The rest? It's just things from outside that we need to deal with, but we were so, so, so happy inside the pitch, and you cannot imagine inside the changing room!"

Enzo Maresca on #ManCity's start to the season: "We need to improve many things, for sure. The way we try to attack, try to defend, no doubt we need to improve things.

"And then in terms of the journey since we started, we won seven or eight in a row, all different for different situations. The last at Anfield was different to the rest for all the situations that happened during the international break, games where we were losing 0-1 vs Bournemouth and we won, the Man United game with 10 players - all different games.

"Winning games, in our job, is the most important thing, but for me it's the day by day, the things I see from the players, that I feel very happy!"

Enzo Maresca on the importance of the #UCL to #ManCity, given it 'might be the last for a while': "I'm just focussed on tomorrow. For sure, the Champions League for this organisation is so, so important - no doubt!

"We're going to try to improve compared to the last two, three years where the club and team struggled a little bit, so we're going to try to do our best to improve from that.

"Then, where we can be in March, April or if this is the last Champions League for a while, I don't know!"

Enzo Maresca: "I'm completely calm, relaxed, I promise you that I stress a lot about game plans and how we can train every day. But I don't stress about things that I don't control, so the message with the players will be exactly the same [as Anfield]: We know how serious is the situation, but at the same time it's not something we can do something [about]. Where we can do some things is inside the pitch, that's why I like to focus there. The message is exactly the same!"

Enzo Maresca on @rubendias' role in the last few days: "Since I joined the club, since the summer, I was in touch with Ruben, also because he was the captain so I needed to speak with him for different reasons. Since day one, he has been a real leader, and he's doing very well in all aspects!"

Enzo Maresca on the #ManCity's post-Liverpool celebrations: "We were very, very happy inside the pitch, sharing time with our fans.

"Probably it has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me. Probably because it's more complicated because if I am an Arsenal fan or a United fan, and you are a @ManCity fan, I can tell you, 'Hey my friend, you cheat', or these kind of things.

"So probably it has been more tough for them, but again, we were happy at the end of the game. Inside the changing room we were very happy, celebrating the three points because we know how difficult it is at Anfield - that's why we were very happy!"
Enzo Maresca is now taking questions from French media, and responding in French. 🇫🇷

Ruben Dias: "Amazing support from our fans [at Anfield], they stood behind us, we will fight for them always until the end, and it was obviously a special feeling to get that win in such a difficult atmosphere, and also because of it being the first game after the international break - which we know, by religion, is always a difficult one!"

Enzo Maresca: "It was a bit strange to be honest, because I think until the first goal we started quite good, we were in the game, we created something, we didn't concede nothing. Then we conceded the first one and after one minute or two minutes, we conceded a second one.

"It's already difficult, but then when you concede two goals in two minutes, it becomes even worse. But at half-time we adjusted something, we didn't lose the balance, and I think second-half we created enough to deserve something more!" [via @footballontnt]

Enzo Maresca: "[At half-time] We adjusted a little the way we were pressing, adjusted something on the ball. I think it's been a bit strange not because of the way we were pressing or attacking, it's been a bit strange because we conceded two in two minutes, and I think we lost a little bit the balance. Enzo Maresca: "Even with 0-3 first-half, I think with the amount of chances we created in the second-half, we deserved something more. And Luis [Enrique] was quite honest [with me] at the end of the game. He said, 'We [PSG] have been quite lucky today!'" [via @footballontnt] https://t.co/76ylmquZzC

Enzo Maresca: "[Against] These kind of teams, if you don't got toe-to-toe, you'll struggle. You have to be brave, you have to go, and in the second-half we were even more in terms of off the ball, pressing, and on the ball also we made some adjustments..."

Enzo Maresca: "I really like to play PSG, to be honest! They're brave, I know the way they want to press, they go, they don't care, man-to-man all over the pitch. On the ball they're quite dynamic! I like to play them!

"I think we're there, to be honest. My feeling is we are there, we are close! The reason why, for me, we struggled first-half is because we conceded two and when you're inside the pitch you know it's already difficult against them, then you think, 'Oh my God!
